cross_post_findings.quote: I bought this a couple years ago here on BaT to teach my son to drive a manual – mission accomplished!
However, now he is in college a couple hours from home, and we agreed that a larger car to haul stuff would be prudent, so now selling this.
I've spent about $3k on it since purchasing it – now has a new clutch, brakes, coils & spark plugs.

(And no, it wasn't my teenager learning the manual that wore out the clutch. The mechanic said the clutch didn't have unusual wear, but something had "let go" which was like a bomb going off in the clutch. The mechanic insisted it was not user error :) )
The service brake light is often on, even though we put on new rotors & pads last year. I suspect one of the brake wear sensors is bad, but the car brakes great so we have never pursued that.

While taking pictures, I noticed the hydraulic struts for the hood were weak, so I have already ordered replacements. Could use some new weatherstriping/seals by the doors. Otherwise, no problems with the car.

provenance.summary: The most consequential finding is the price history: the same VIN sold on Bring a Trailer on 2024-04-20 for $11,000 (Hagerty records $11,550 including fee) at 76k miles, and it is back on BaT at no reserve on 2026-09-07 with 90k miles and bidding only at $1,750 with six days to run. Seller Tpetty confirms the chain — "I bought this a couple years ago here on BaT to teach my son to drive a manual" — and is selling because the son is away at college and the family wants a larger car; he says he has spent about $3k on a new clutch, brakes, coils and spark plugs. Notable disclosed faults: the clutch and hydraulic cylinders failed and were replaced in July 2024 (his mechanic said 'something had let go... like a bomb going off in the clutch'), the service brake light is 'often on' despite new rotors and pads and has never been diagnosed, the hood struts are weak with parts on order, and the door weatherstripping needs replacing. The car carries an April 2019 Carfax 'minor damage' entry to the front/right front, paintwork on one bumper cover, a torn driver's seat bolster, visible underside rust, at least one open recall, five previous owners and a Carfax last-reported odometer of 78,332 — plus failed 2021 and 2022 emissions tests that the prior seller attributed to battery disconnection and insufficient drive cycles. One documentation inconsistency: the 2024 listing called the paint Le Mans Blue Metallic (381) while the 2026 listing calls it Montego Blue Metallic (A51), with no repaint disclosed. No other sale attempts, withdrawals or private listings for this VIN surfaced in web, forum, Facebook, eBay or Reddit searches.

critical_evidence.evidence: The listing details clutch and hydraulics (July 2024), plugs and coils (September 2024), brakes (2025), rear shock mounts and a pre-sale oil change — but says nothing about the electric water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, or hoses on a 16-year-old, 90k-mile N52. Silence here is unknown, not good.

No statement about oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket or oil-pan gasket condition. The attached engine-bay photo is a top-down view over the plastic cover and does not show the OFHG area or the back of the block; the underside photo shown is the rear suspension, not the oil pan.

documentation.rationale: Carfax is included and BaT provenance is traceable (sold to this seller 4/20/2024 for $11,000), and specific recent work is named with dates: clutch and hydraulics July 2024, plugs and coils September 2024, brakes 2025. But the seller himself calls the records 'partial,' the April 2019 front/right-front damage has no repair documentation, the ECU tune has no brand/dyno/file provenance, and the two model-critical files — cooling and oil leaks — are entirely absent.

condition.rationale: Real positives: fresh clutch, fresh brakes, new coils and plugs, rear shock mounts done, Bilstein/Eibach suspension. Against that, the listing itself discloses a service brake light that is often on and has never been diagnosed, a torn driver's seat bolster, bumper-cover paintwork over a Carfax damage entry, tired door weatherstripping, weak hood struts, and 'rust visible on underside components' — the underside photo shows heavy surface corrosion on rear suspension hardware typical of a Midwest car. Cooling and oil-leak condition are unexamined, which pulls this down further.

price_value.rationale: No reserve with a $1,750 opening bid and seven days to run; the only comp given is a 2012 Sport with 57k miles at $15,500 (Cars & Bids, April 2026), and this car sold for $11,000 in April 2024 with 13k fewer miles, before the tune/intake/exhaust were a resale question and before the accident-free premium mattered. A realistic landing zone in the high-$8k to low-$12k range would sit at or below the $10-13k target, but the tune, the Midwest underside, five prior owners, and the disclosed damage entry all compress resale in 6-24 months — the thing the mission explicitly cares about.

mission_fit.rationale: On paper this is the exact profile car: manual N52 128i coupe, deliberately chosen by the seller over the turbo 135i for the same reason Jason is leaving the 335i. It fails the 'stock powertrain' half of the brief — aftermarket ECU tune plus intake — and appears not to be a Sport/M Sport car. Add a live brake warning lamp and an undocumented cooling system and it is a bridge that needs work before it is trustworthy, not a turn-key one.

logistics.rationale: Quincy, IL is a long fly-and-drive from Carmel and that is purely a cost item — roughly $1,200-$2,000 in transport or a two-and-a-half day drive Jason has said he will do. The real logistics issue is timing: a PPI must be booked and completed before the 9/13 close, PPI access is not addressed in the listing, and BaT payment moves fast. California registration with a tuned DME and non-CARB intake is an extra step that needs the stock file and stock intake to exist.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Montego Blue over black with a manual, sunroof, no nav screen, Bilstein/Eibach and a strut brace is a genuinely appealing E82 spec, and the shape looks clean and well-kept in the photos. It loses points for leatherette rather than sport seats, the apparent lack of the Sport package Jason's profile asks for, and a modification set that reads as previous-owner taste rather than a factory point of view.

positives: Correct mission hardware: naturally aspirated N52 with a six-speed manual in an E82 coupe — precisely the anti-335i drivetrain, and the seller says he chose it for that reason.

Recent wear items are done and dated: clutch and hydraulic cylinders July 2024, ignition coils and spark plugs September 2024, brake rotors and pads 2025, rear shock mounts under prior ownership, oil change pre-sale.
No reserve on BaT with traceable provenance — the same car sold publicly here for $11,000 in April 2024 — so the market, not a seller's number, sets the price.
Unusually candid seller disclosure: brake light, weak hood struts, weatherstripping, seat tear, bumper paint, underside rust and the clutch failure story are all volunteered.
Attractive, coherent spec — Montego Blue, no nav, manual, sunroof, Bilstein B6/Eibach — that shows well in the exterior and side photos.
concerns: Observed: the service brake light is 'often on' and has never been diagnosed; the seller assumes a wear sensor. A live warning lamp on a car you are buying sight-unseen at auction is an open fault until a scan says otherwise.

Observed: the powertrain is not stock — aftermarket ECU tune plus aftermarket intake, with no tune brand, no dyno, no stated stock DME file. That conflicts with the profile's stock-powertrain requirement, complicates California smog/registration, and narrows the resale pool in 6-24 months.
Observed: Carfax 'minor damage' front and right front (April 2019) with no detail, plus paintwork on a bumper cover and no repair invoices; and a disclosed torn driver's seat bolster.

Observed: 'rust is visible on underside components,' and the underside photo shows heavily corroded rear suspension hardware — an Illinois car with road-salt exposure, which means seized fasteners and higher labor on any future suspension or subframe work.

Unverified: no electric water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or hose history at 16 years and 90k miles (ask for receipts by date and mileage; if none, budget the pump/thermostat and cooling plastics as near-term).

Unverified: no statement on oil-filter-housing, valve-cover or oil-pan leaks, and a fresh pre-sale oil change can mask a wet block (request cold photos of the OFHG area and the underside of the pan on a lift).

seller_questions: Do you have any receipt for the electric water pump or thermostat, and if so what date and odometer reading? If not, has either ever been replaced to your knowledge?
Has the coolant expansion tank or any coolant hose been replaced, and does the tank hold level between top-ups — when did you last add coolant?

Which tune is loaded in the DME (brand, version), and do you have the stock file or a stock DME/intake to include with the car so it can be returned to factory configuration for California registration?
Can you photograph the oil-filter-housing area and the oil pan from below on a lift, before the car is washed, so leak paths are visible?
Will you plug in a scan tool and send photos of all stored fault codes, including the brake system module, plus current adaptation and readiness status?
What are the DOT date codes on all four Continental tires, and what is the measured tread depth at each corner?
Which recall does Carfax show as open, and can a BMW dealer print the open-campaign list for this VIN?
Can you post the actual invoices for the July 2024 clutch job, the September 2024 coils and plugs, and the 2025 brake service, with mileages?
What did the shop find when the clutch 'let go' — was the flywheel, slave cylinder or release bearing replaced, and is that itemized on the invoice?
Will you allow an independent BMW shop in the Quincy area to put the car on a lift for a pre-purchase inspection before the auction ends, and can you deliver it to them?
Have the hood struts been installed yet, and would you fit the door weatherstripping before delivery?
Has any rustproofing or undercoating work been done, and are there photos of the rear subframe mounts and floor pans from below?
ppi_focus: Cooling system: pressure-test the expansion tank and hoses cold, verify electric water pump operation and coolant temperature control under load, and check pump/thermostat part date stamps
Oil leaks: inspect oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket and oil-pan gasket on a lift after degrease, and check the alternator bracket area for oil contamination
Full fault-code scan of all modules with attention to the brake module (the disclosed service brake light) and DME adaptations reflecting the tune
Underside corrosion survey: rear subframe mounting points, trailing-arm bushings, brake and fuel lines, exhaust hangers, and whether fasteners are seizing
Front and right-front structure: check radiator support, inner fender, headlight mounts and bumper reinforcement for the April 2019 damage, plus paint depth readings on all panels
Clutch and manual gearbox: engagement point, pedal feel, no shudder, verify July 2024 work quality and check for rear-main or gearbox seal seepage
Suspension: condition of the Bilstein/Eibach setup, front control-arm bushings and rear shock mounts, plus ride height and any bind from the aftermarket springs
Valvetronic/VANOS operation and cold-start noise on the N52; verify no lifter tick or eccentric shaft sensor codes
Tire date codes, tread depth, and confirmation all four match
Verify open recall status at a BMW dealer, especially the PCV heater and airbag inflator campaigns
what_would_change_verdict: Receipts showing the electric water pump, thermostat and expansion tank replaced within the last few years would remove the largest unknown and move this up materially.

A clean independent PPI on a lift confirming no oil-filter-housing or pan leaks, sound structure at the right front, and surface-only underside rust would justify bidding to the low end of the expected range.
The seller including the stock DME file and factory intake — making a return to CARB-legal configuration a same-day job — would resolve the California registration risk and the resale drag.
A scan proving the brake lamp is a simple wear sensor, with a quote to fix, would convert an open fault into a $200 line item.
If no PPI can be arranged before the 9/13 close, or if the scan shows cooling/oil-leak codes or structural repair at the right front, walk away regardless of price.
evidence.mission_note: This is the right shape of car for the enthusiast-bridge mission — manual, naturally aspirated N52, rear-drive, cheap to exit — and at no reserve it should land inside the $10-13k target. But the tune plus intake, an undiagnosed brake warning light, an undocumented cooling system and a salted Midwest underside make it a project-adjacent bridge rather than a turn-key one, and in accelerated_bridge mode that matters.
evidence.rationale: The result is a conditional yes only with a lift-based PPI and cooling documentation before the 9/13 close. The mechanicals that usually kill these cars have partly been addressed and dated: clutch and hydraulics July 2024, coils and plugs September 2024, brakes 2025, rear shock mounts under prior ownership — and the seller specifically bought an N52 to avoid turbo complexity, the same logic driving Jason away from the 335i. Against that, the listing itself discloses an undiagnosed service brake lamp that is 'often on,' a Carfax front/right-front damage entry from April 2019 with no repair documentation plus bumper-cover paintwork, a torn driver's seat bolster, and 'rust visible on underside components' that the underside photo confirms as heavy surface corrosion on the rear suspension hardware. The two model-critical files — electric water pump/thermostat/expansion tank history and oil-filter-housing/valve-cover/pan leak status — are entirely absent, and a pre-sale oil change makes visual leak assessment harder, so both must be treated as unknown and budgeted. The aftermarket ECU tune and intake break the profile's stock-powertrain requirement, create a California smog and registration step, and will cost money on resale in the 6-24 month window the mission cares about. Provenance is at least honest and traceable: same car, $11,000 on BaT in April 2024, 13k miles ago. At no reserve with $1,750 bid and a week to run, the price should stay in range, but the all-in should be figured with roughly $1,100-$3,200 of known work plus transport from Quincy, IL on top of the hammer.
evidence.next_action: Before bidding, book an independent BMW specialist near Quincy, IL for a lift PPI plus full module scan this week, and ask the seller in the comments for cooling-system receipts and confirmation that a stock DME file and factory intake come with the car.
